blocks.title: Predict: convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
content: If $2^5=32$, what question is $\log_2(32)$ answering?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
content: $\log_b(x)=y$ means exactly $b^y=x$.
The logarithm is the exponent.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
content: Convert $\log_4(64)=3$ and $4^{-3}=1/64$ between forms.
steps: The base remains 4 and the logarithm records the exponent.

blocks.title: You Try: convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
content: Rewrite $5^3=125$, $3^{-2}=1/9$, and $\ln(7)=x$ in the opposite form.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
content: Keep the base unchanged.
The log argument becomes the exponential result.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: convert between logarithmic and exponential forms
content: Complete the sentence: a logarithm tells us ____.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: evaluate and simplify logarithmic expressions
content: Without a calculator, evaluate $\log_2(32)$ and $\ln(1)$.
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: evaluate and simplify logarithmic expressions
content: Common log has base 10; natural log has base e.
$\log_b(1)=0$, $\log_b(b)=1$, and $\log_b(b^x)=x$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: evaluate and simplify logarithmic expressions
content: Evaluate $\log(250)$ and $\ln(40)$, then verify by exponentiating.
steps: The inverse checks confirm both calculator entries.

blocks.title: You Try: evaluate and simplify logarithmic expressions
content: Simplify $\log_7(1)$, $\ln(e^{-5/2})$, and $e^{\ln 7}$.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: evaluate and simplify logarithmic expressions
content: A logarithm of a number between 0 and 1 is negative when the base exceeds 1.
Logs undo exponents only when bases match.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: evaluate and simplify logarithmic expressions
content: Name two inverse identities involving logarithms and exponents.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: graph logarithmic functions and determine their domains
content: What feature of an exponential graph becomes the vertical asymptote of its inverse?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: graph logarithmic functions and determine their domains
content: Logarithmic graphs reflect exponential graphs across $y=x$.
For $f(x)=\log_b(g(x))$, require $g(x)>0$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: graph logarithmic functions and determine their domains
content: Transform $y=\log_2(x)$ into $f(x)=\log_2(x+1)+2$.
Shift the parent graph left 1 and up 2.
Domain: $(-1,\infty)$; vertical asymptote: $x=-1$.
Intercepts: $(0,2)$ and $(-3/4,0)$.
verification: Verify transformed graph features and domain inequalities.
steps: Shift the parent graph left 1 and up 2.

assets.alt: Graph of f of x equals log base 2 of x plus 1, plus 2, with vertical asymptote x equals negative 1 and labeled intercepts

blocks.title: You Try: graph logarithmic functions and determine their domains
content: Find the domain and vertical asymptote of $\log(3x-6)$.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: graph logarithmic functions and determine their domains
content: The logarithm argument must be strictly positive, not merely nonnegative.
Horizontal shifts move the vertical asymptote.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify transformed graph features and domain inequalities.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: graph logarithmic functions and determine their domains
content: Explain how to find a logarithmic domain before graphing.

blocks.title: Predict: solve logarithmic and exponential equations using inverse properties
content: When should you convert to exponential form, and when should you take a logarithm?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: solve logarithmic and exponential equations using inverse properties
content: Use exponential form for a single logarithm.
Use one-to-one properties when equal logs have the same base.
Use change of base: $\log_a(x)=\log(x)/\log(a)$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: solve logarithmic and exponential equations using inverse properties
content: Solve $\log_2(x-5)=4$ and evaluate $\log_4(25)$.
verification: Recalculate equation solutions and change-of-base values.
steps: Substitution and exponentiation verify both results.

blocks.title: You Try: solve logarithmic and exponential equations using inverse properties
content: Solve $3^x=175$ and evaluate $\log_3(50)$.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: solve logarithmic and exponential equations using inverse properties
content: Reject solutions that make a log argument nonpositive.
The log of a sum is not the sum of logs.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Recalculate equation solutions and change-of-base values.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: solve logarithmic and exponential equations using inverse properties
content: Write a two-step checklist for solving and checking a logarithmic equation.
